about: Expected case-runner failures on the one compiler (scripts/cases.mjs). Each entry names cases (an id relative to tests/, a glob, or a list), the lanes it covers (the --lanes syntax; omitted means all), why they fail, and the plan task that owns the fix (docs/migration/index.md). A failure not covered here fails the run; an entry that covers no failure any more is reported for removal. Recorded from the pre-M1 binary ~/lilscript-work/bin/pre-m1/lilscript (sha256 01c5e298...) on 2026-09-24: 29 failing cases, all harvested regressions; the 72 tests/cases programs and tests/modules pass on every lane.

entries.reason: `export constructor` is refused: "direct module checking does not yet support nominal constructor exports".

Name-keyed host helper: the old route lowered the extern `objectHasOwn` to Object.hasOwn by its name; the one compiler gives extern names no meaning (dropped by design), so the program throws "objectHasOwn is not defined". The case's prelude must declare the binding (`globalThis.objectHasOwn = Object.hasOwn`).
entries.owner: M1.5 (the harvested case gets a declared binding; M10.2 owns the host catalog)

entries.reason: `public_aggregate_abi = "positional"` is ignored: the instance reaches the host as {value:7}, so `slot[0]` is undefined. M1.4 refuses the key at load; these cases then become refusal cases.
Two faults: `public_aggregate_abi = "positional"` is ignored, and a field default (`new Map`) is evaluated before a constructor argument (D3.4 order).
A struct value passed to an extern is refused: Unsupported "foreign value-struct storage adaptation".
Expectation conflict: the test expects the inferred wrapper name 'handle'; docs/language-v0.1.md says adapter wrappers stay anonymous, and the compiler follows the spec here.
entries.owner: M1.9 (decide the rule, then fix the case or the compiler)

entries.reason: The sibling of the -aggregate case: formation-only keeps the wrapper anonymous (the spec's rule, against the test's expectation); production gives it a name and passes.
entries.owner: M1.9 (decide the rule, then fix the case or the compiler)

entries.reason: Refused, not miscompiled: a struct union widened to JsValue, a generic function taking a struct ("generic product transport requires a complete private interface" on scripts) and a generic body that does not return its parameter ("generic product body requires closed value forwarding" on modules).
entries.owner: M1.9 (the struct-to-host family; the plan does not yet name this gap)

entries.reason: Native `Record<T>` is refused ("native source type", "native callable payload type").
A self-recursive closure is refused natively: "native captured dynamic callable payload".
entries.owner: M11.6 (the portable subset; the plan's list does not yet name closures)
